test.name: Differently-surnamed household head is flagged as a FAN lead, not dismissed as a boardinghouse
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_014: the record the user pasted is now served as a record_read fixture (the 1860 census household of Silas Kerrigan, Schuylkill County, with the Flynns in it), and extraction runs in code. An 1860-style census household where the subject's family (the Flynns) is enumerated inside a household headed by a man with a different surname (Silas Kerrigan, b. ~1798). The skill must extract the household faithfully AND surface the head as possible kin — the ~24-year age gap to Mary Flynn makes a parent-child relationship plausible, and 'Kerrigan' a candidate maiden name worth investigating — as a lead for hypothesis-tracking, rather than silently assuming a boardinghouse or asserting a specific relationship the record doesn't support. Guards the 'differently-surnamed household head is a FAN lead' rule.

judge_context: Override for Correctness and Completeness: this suite reuses one project scenario for every record, so the record is usually about people other than the project's objective (e.g. a Becker or Ferber record in a Patrick Flynn project). That mismatch is intended and is not an error by the skill. Do not lower any score because the record concerns someone else.

The skill makes one extraction_append call with the record id and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
